text:
sam_sales: Hey team — FinBank asked if we can pin a specific model variant per region and define a clear fallback path. They want `mistral-v2-2026-01` pinned in EU for compliance and SLA, but in APAC they'd accept a quantized variant. Can we confirm: (1) how pinning works across Hosted vs Dedicated, (2) what fallback routing looks like, and (3) audit/logging for the exact served model?
sarah_pm: @sam_sales thanks — quick clarifying q: is FinBank asking for model pin *and* geo gating so only EU traffic sees the pinned version? or just prefer EU pinning if available? :eyes:

sam_sales: They want EU traffic to always hit the pinned version (no silent fallback to newer versions). APAC can fallback to a smaller quantized variant when capacity/latency dictates. They also need proof of what was served for each request (audit) for compliance.
alex_p: short answer: we support model pinning per-catalog-entry and routing by region. For Hosted the control plane enforces pin at routing time; for Dedicated, customers can pin on the deployment manifest. Fallback behavior is policy-driven (failover vs degrade).
maya_infra: a few notes on constraints: (a) pinned model consumes capacity like any other — pinning to a specific GPU pool may require dedicated capacity reservation; (b) geo gating uses request region metadata + routing policy. We'll need a capacity check for EU pool.
jordan_ml: quantized variant compatibility warning: not all operator stacks are identical. If APAC wants a `quant` variant as fallback, we must ensure the fallback model matches output signature & tokenizer. Otherwise you'll get subtle regressions.
sarah_pm: good call. Sam — can you ask FinBank whether deterministic outputs across variants is a hard req or if small distribution changes are acceptable?
sam_sales: I'll confirm, but they said compliance > parity. They want explicit model served logs, timestamps, and rollout audit.
lia_eng: For rollout + rollback UX: Console can pin a model version for a catalog entry and we can expose a `strict_pin` toggle that disables automatic upgrades and auto-fallback to newer model versions. Example config we can push to prod and expose in the API:```yaml
catalog_entry: mistral-v2
routes:
  - region: eu
    model: mistral-v2-2026-01
    strict_pin: true
  - region: apac
    model: mistral-v2-2025-11-quant
    fallback: true
policies:
  fallback_policy: degraded-response
  audit: request-model-id
```
lia_eng: Implementation notes: add `strict_pin` flag, ensure router uses pinned mapping before dynamic model selection. Also include the served-model header in responses and wire to audit logs.

alex_p: routing-wise we can implement two-level resolution: (1) catalog pin map, (2) per-request routing policy (latency/cost). If `strict_pin` true -> skip step (2). We'll need an infra ticket to allocate an EU pool if FinBank requires Dedicated.
maya_infra: allocation ticket + capacity calc needed. Also KMS/per-region key access for logging if they want encrypted audit logs — legal/security must sign off.
deploy-bot: deploy: rollouts/2026-03/pin-routing-feature started by @lia_eng — canary to eu-dev cluster
jordan_ml: also recommend adding a smoke eval to compare pinned vs fallback outputs on a small prompt set. We can gate rollout on no-major-regressions.
sarah_pm: Launch criteria (proposal): 1) Router supports `strict_pin` and fallback policy, 2) Served-model audit header exists and logs to audit sink, 3) Capacity/reservation path documented for Dedicated, 4) Smoke eval pass, 5) Security sign-off on encrypted logs.
sam_sales: perfect. I'll loop FinBank in and get confirmation on parity vs compliance. Also ask whether they want Dedicated reservation or Hosted with SLA.
lia_eng: I'll follow up with a short RFC in #eng-platform with config schema and API changes. ETA: mock API by EOW.
maya_infra: I'll start a capacity calc for EU pool and estimate cost.
alex_p: tagging @jordan_ml for eval harness. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
sam_sales: thanks all — will update when I hear back from FinBank.
